Gibeon
GIB-ee-uhn
proper noun (place)
Hebrew Gibon, a major town of the Hivites north of Jerusalem; the home of the Gibeonites who deceived Joshua, and the great high place where the tabernacle stood and Solomon sought wisdom.

See also: Gibeon

📖 Biblical Definition

Gibeon was a notable city north of Jerusalem, prominent in Israel's history at several turns. Its inhabitants, the Gibeonites, fearing destruction, deceived Joshua and the elders with worn clothes and mouldy bread into making a league of peace; when the ruse was discovered, Israel kept its oath but made them "hewers of wood and drawers of water" for the house of God (Josh 9). When five Amorite kings attacked Gibeon for this league, Joshua came to its defense, and the LORD cast down great hailstones and made the sun stand still over Gibeon until Israel was avenged (Josh 10:11-13). At the pool of Gibeon, Abner's and Joab's men fought their deadly contest (2 Sam 2:12-17), and there Joab later murdered Amasa (2 Sam 20:8-10). After the ark was moved, the tabernacle of the LORD and the brazen altar remained at Gibeon, "the great high place," and there Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings; the LORD appeared to him by night and gave him the wise and understanding heart he asked for above riches and long life (1 Kings 3:4-12; 2 Chr 1:3-12). Gibeon stands in the dictionary as the city of the kept oath, the standing sun, and the gift of wisdom — a place where God honored Israel's faithfulness to its word and answered the prayer for understanding.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A major town north of Jerusalem (Josh 9-10): home of the Gibeonites who deceived Joshua into a league Israel honored, the place where the sun stood still, and the great high place where Solomon offered sacrifice and received his wise and understanding heart (1 Kings 3).

GIBEON, proper noun. A major town of the Hivites north of Jerusalem.

Home of the Gibeonites, who deceived Joshua into a league of peace (Josh 9).

Where the LORD cast down hailstones and the sun stood still (Josh 10:11-13).

The site of the pool where Abner's and Joab's men fought (2 Sam 2:12-17).

The great high place where Solomon sacrificed and received wisdom (1 Kings 3:4-12).

📖 Key Scripture

Josh 9:15 — "And Joshua made peace with them, and made a league with them, to let them live: and the princes of the congregation sware unto them."

Josh 10:13 — "And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the people had avenged themselves upon their enemies. Is not this written in the book of Jasher? So the sun stood still in the midst of heaven, and hasted not to go down about a whole day."

1 Kings 3:5 — "In Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream by night: and God said, Ask what I shall give thee."

2 Chr 1:3 — "So Solomon, and all the congregation with him, went to the high place that was at Gibeon; for there was the tabernacle of the congregation of God, which Moses the servant of the LORD had made in the wilderness."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Gibeon is corrupted when the sun standing still is dismissed as myth, or when the binding force of Israel's oath to the Gibeonites is treated as primitive scruple rather than the seriousness of a vow before God.

expand to see more

Miracle-denied misreading. Naturalism explains away the long day at Gibeon as legend or poetic exaggeration. Scripture records it as a real act of the God who rules the heavens, answering Joshua's bold prayer. The dictionary holds the miracle as written: the Maker of the sun is free to govern it as He wills, and the God who parted the sea and raised the dead is not constrained by the ordinary course He Himself ordained. To strip Gibeon of its wonder is to deny the Lord of creation.

Oath-trivialized misreading. Modern readers often think Israel foolish to keep a league won by deception. Scripture treats the sworn oath as sacred: because the princes had sworn by the LORD, the covenant stood, and centuries later God sent famine on the land for Saul's breach of it (2 Sam 21:1-2). The dictionary recovers the weight of a vow before God: an oath in His name binds the conscience, and faithfulness to one's word, even when costly, honors the God who is Himself faithful.
